description:
Compute validation once per captured repository image and derive every validation view from that one report. Per-issue, scope and `--explain` validation and the built-in gate checkers currently run their own copies of the same passes, disagree in what they read, and the per-issue view is three times slower than validating the whole repository.

## Background

Whole-repository `jit validate` runs `validation::repository::validate_repository` over a captured image. The other views run separate pipelines:

- **Executor copies.** Per-issue validation (`run_rules`, `crates/jit/src/commands/validate.rs:2019`), `--scope` (`validate_scope`, `validate.rs:2213`) and `--explain` (`explain_rules`, `validate.rs:2373`) read through storage and the executor's disk-backed caches. They use executor-side copies of the dangling-link pass (`validate.rs:1599` against `validation/repository.rs:766`), the enforcement-drift pass (`validate.rs:1702,1742` against `repository.rs:608`) and the review-placeholder pass (`validate.rs:2146` against `repository.rs:700`).
- **Gate-checker copies.** `captured_issue_rule_report` and `captured_scope_rule_report` (`crates/jit/src/commands/gate_check.rs:457,527`) repeat the per-issue and scope logic over the image. Each then runs the full `validate_repository` (`gate_check.rs:450`) only to keep its dangling-link and drift findings. `rule_validation_report` repeats the same setup prelude a third time.
- **Inverted dependency.** `validation/repository.rs` imports the rule-name constants, `find_planning_node`, `planning_node_plan_path` and `validate_claims_index_at` from `commands` (`repository.rs:550,630,715,751-752,838,896`).

Measured costs on a copy of this repository (1,170 issues, about 1,160 qualified link labels, release build):

- **Per-issue validation.** `jit validate <id>` takes 2.36 s; whole-repository `jit validate` takes 0.80 s. The per-issue path resolves every link label in the repository through `show_item` (`crates/jit/src/commands/item.rs:327`), re-resolving the item kinds (one regex compile per kind, `item.rs:72`) and the aggregated issue index for each label, and only then filters to the one issue.
- **Quadratic capture discovery.** `discover_document_references` (`validate.rs:1259`) calls `CaptureSpec::discover_paths` once per document reference. Each call clones the spec and revalidates every requested path (`crates/jit/src/repository_state/image.rs:653-665,761-790`), and the discover closure re-applies `base(spec)` every round (`validate.rs:397`). With 541 references over a spec of more than 1,200 paths, `CaptureSpec::validate` is about 20% of the inclusive validate profile, and capture runs twice per validate.
- **Repeated parsing.** Whole-repository validation parses every issue file four times through three issue loaders (`validate.rs:453,684,1037`; `repository.rs:366`), and the index through three readers. Local rule evaluation creates a `SchemaEngine` per issue (`crates/jit/src/validation/local.rs:317`), so every JSON Schema recompiles for every issue.
- **Issue create warnings.** Human-mode `issue create` lists every issue and evaluates every graph rule after the mutation commits, to print warnings for the one new issue (`crates/jit/src/main.rs:3071-3077`). That recaptures a whole validation image: 373 ms against 55 ms with `--quiet`. The JSON path computes no warnings at all.
- **Fix mode.** `validate --fix` runs a full validation first and discards the result in fix mode (`validate.rs:45`), then publishes each hierarchy fix and each readiness correction as its own mutation.
- **Link checking.** Document link checking probes external URLs serially, with a new HTTP agent per asset and no deduplication (`crates/jit/src/commands/document.rs:1012-1016,1192`).

Smaller duplication sits on the same paths. Plan-document resolution is written three times (`validate.rs:1276,1335`; `repository.rs:726`). The content-format default chain appears at 9 sites and the strictness chain at 3.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Exactly one function computes the validation report: a pure function in the validation layer that takes a captured repository image and produces the whole-repository report.
- [hard] REQ-02: Whole-repository, single-issue, container-scope, single-rule and `--explain` validation are each that report filtered by a selection. None of them reads repository state outside the one captured image.
- [hard] REQ-03: The built-in validation gate checkers report the selected subset of the same report. For a given image, each checker's findings equal the findings `jit validate` reports for the same selection.
- [hard] REQ-04: One test owns the selection contract: for generated images and selections, the selected report equals the whole report restricted to that selection.
- [hard] REQ-05: No executor-side copy of the dangling-link, enforcement-drift or review-placeholder pass remains, and no gate checker calls whole-repository validation to extract a subset of its findings.
- [hard] REQ-06: The validation layer imports nothing from `commands`. Rule names and planning-node resolution live in the validation or domain layer, and the claims-index check receives its inputs from its caller.
- [hard] REQ-07: Item-link findings resolve every label against one address index built once per report, with item kinds resolved once per report.
- [hard] REQ-08: On this repository, measured with a release build, `jit validate <id>` takes no longer than whole-repository `jit validate`.
- [hard] REQ-09: Adding paths to a capture spec validates only the added entries, and validation requests all document-reference paths of a capture round as one batch.
- [hard] REQ-10: A whole-repository validation parses the index and each issue file once, through one loader, and every pass consumes those parsed issues.
- [hard] REQ-11: Each JSON Schema in the rule set compiles once per report.
- [hard] REQ-12: One function resolves plan-document references for every caller, and the content-format and strictness defaults each come from one configuration accessor.
- [hard] REQ-13: `issue create` derives its advisory findings for the new issue from the image its mutation captured, reports the same findings in human and JSON output, and performs no repository read or capture after the mutation publishes.
- [hard] REQ-14: `validate --fix` computes no report before deriving its fixes, publishes every fix through one mutation, and always reports the result of one report computed after the fixes, including when it applied none.
- [hard] REQ-15: Document link checking probes each distinct external URL once per run, through one HTTP agent with a request timeout and bounded concurrency.

## Notes

- Serves `@/charter/D-20` (one computation per capability) and `@/charter/D-18` (unify mechanism rather than add it).
- Restores `@/inv/convention-convergence` and `@/inv/architecture-dependency-direction`.
- REQ-04 follows `@/inv/orthogonal-tests`: the selection behavior is proven once against the report, and each view proves only its wiring.
title: Compute one validation report and derive every validation view from it
